Shared steps of the geography assignment functions

Source: R/utils-geography.R
validate_geography_cols.Rd

Internal helpers shared by assign_treating_geography() and assign_facility_geography().

Usage

validate_geography_cols(
  verbose,
  do_region,
  do_zip,
  region_col_str,
  hosp_region_col_str,
  zip_col_str,
  hosp_zip_col_str,
  check_zip_col = TRUE
)

resolve_geography_output_col(
  new_col,
  data,
  overwrite,
  reserved_col,
  arg_name,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

assign_geography_reassignment(
  data,
  do_region,
  do_zip,
  region_col_str,
  hosp_region_col_str,
  zip_col_str,
  hosp_zip_col_str,
  region_output_col_str,
  zip_output_col_str,
  region_target_exists,
  zip_target_exists,
  preserve_original_geographies,
  mask
)

patient_geography(data, col_str)

resolve_geography_sources(
  data,
  region_sym,
  hosp_region_sym,
  zip_sym,
  hosp_zip_sym
)

resolve_geography_outputs(
  data,
  flags,
  new_region_col,
  new_zip_col,
  overwrite,
  reserved_col,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

reassign_geography(
  data,
  flags,
  sources,
  outputs,
  preserve_original_geographies,
  mask
)

warn_site_without_region_match(data, region_col_str, site)

flag_out_of_state(data, region_col_str, site)

inform_treating_result(data, outputs, verbose)

inform_facility_result(data, outputs, verbose)

Arguments

verbose

Logical. Whether to emit informational messages.

do_region, do_zip

Logical. Whether region/zip geography is being processed.

region_col_str, hosp_region_col_str, zip_col_str, hosp_zip_col_str

Resolved column names (strings), or NULL when the optional column is absent.

check_zip_col

Logical. Whether to validate zip_col_str (the patient zip column) here.

new_col

The user-supplied output column name, or NULL.

data

A data frame.

overwrite

Logical. Whether an existing column may be overwritten.

reserved_col

The dot-prefixed bookkeeping column name the output must not collide with.

arg_name

The calling function's argument name (for example "new_region_col"), used in error messages.

call

The environment errors are attributed to; see resolve_col().

region_output_col_str, zip_output_col_str

Resolved output column names from resolve_geography_output_col(), or NULL.

region_target_exists, zip_target_exists

Logical. Whether the output column already existed in data.

preserve_original_geographies

Logical. Whether to add original_region/original_zip_code columns.

mask

Logical vector, one element per row of data: which rows are reassigned.

col_str

A resolved column name, or NULL when the column is absent.

region_sym, hosp_region_sym, zip_sym, hosp_zip_sym

Symbols captured from the four source column arguments (raw ESSENCE or snake_case names).

flags

The list returned by validate_geography_cols(), with do_region and do_zip.

new_region_col, new_zip_col

The user-supplied output column names, or NULL to skip that geography type.

sources

The list returned by resolve_geography_sources().

outputs

The list returned by resolve_geography_outputs().

site

The site prefix identifying in-state Region values.

Value

validate_geography_cols() returns a list with do_region and do_zip. resolve_geography_sources() returns a list with region, hosp_region, zip, and hosp_zip (strings or NULL). resolve_geography_outputs() returns a list with region and zip (strings or NULL). reassign_geography() and flag_out_of_state() return the updated data frame. warn_site_without_region_match() and inform_*_result() are called for their conditions. resolve_geography_output_col() returns the normalized output column name, or NULL. assign_geography_reassignment() returns data with the geography columns written. patient_geography() returns the patient column's values, or a single NA when the column is absent.

Details

validate_geography_cols() downgrades do_region/do_zip to FALSE (with an informational message) when a column required for that geography type is absent. The facility columns (HospitalRegion, HospitalZip) are always required for their type. The patient columns (Region, ZipCode) are only the "leave this row alone" values of a selective reassignment, so whether they are required depends on the caller. This function never validates Region: assign_treating_geography() checks it separately afterward, since it is unconditionally required there for out-of-state detection regardless of which geography types are requested, and assign_facility_geography() never reads it. check_zip_col says whether to validate ZipCode here: assign_treating_geography() needs it, while assign_facility_geography() reassigns every row, so it never reads the patient columns (unless overwrite = TRUE names one as its output).

resolve_geography_output_col() resolves a new_region_col/new_zip_col argument (a plain string naming the output column, or NULL to skip that geography type) to its janitor::clean_names()-normalized form. It aborts if the name collides with reserved_col, the bookkeeping column (.out_of_state/.facility_geography) the calling function itself adds, which would silently break the return-value contract. reserved_col is passed dot-prefixed, as it is referenced everywhere else, but janitor::make_clean_names() always strips a leading dot, so the comparison strips it from reserved_col too. It also aborts if the resolved name already exists in data unless overwrite = TRUE, which is what makes writing to a new column non-destructive by default and requires an explicit opt-in before any existing column can be clobbered.

The remaining helpers are the stages the two exported functions share: resolve_geography_sources() resolves the four optional source columns to strings (or NULL when absent); resolve_geography_outputs() resolves both output column names with resolve_geography_output_col(); reassign_geography() works out which output columns already exist and calls assign_geography_reassignment(). Only assign_treating_geography() uses warn_site_without_region_match() (a site that matches no Region value, such as a typo, the wrong case, or another state's pull, would otherwise flag every visit as out-of-state without any sign that something is off) and flag_out_of_state(). "{site}_UNKNOWN" (for example "KY_UNKNOWN") is ESSENCE's placeholder for a known-site record whose residential geography could not be determined; unlike "OTHER_REGION" it carries the site prefix, so it must be tested for explicitly or the prefix check would leave it classified as in-state. inform_treating_result() and inform_facility_result() report the outcome.

assign_geography_reassignment() applies the "preserve original values, then reassign from the hospital columns" logic common to both functions. mask marks which rows are reassigned: assign_treating_geography() passes .out_of_state (selective), assign_facility_geography() an all-TRUE vector (universal). The *_target_exists flags say whether the output column already held a value (which resolve_geography_output_col() only allows with overwrite = TRUE); original_region/original_zip_code are only added in that case, since writing to a genuinely new column already leaves the original untouched. They are populated only where mask is TRUE, so an unmodified row is always identifiable by is.na(original_region).
